summary: This figure from the Syncopate paper compares three backends for realizing the same chunk-level communication schedule generated by the compiler. Panel (a) shows communication issued by a dedicated copy engine with global-memory signaling: tiles produced by compute SMs signal readiness to separate RS Kernel units. Panel (b) shows a dedicated SM (running TMA/CUDA) driving the transfer as RS Chunk units, again via global-memory signaling. Panel (c) shows communication co-located with compute on the same SM, using a faster shared-memory barrier to hand tiles to RS Tile units. All three panels share an identical internal structure (an SM/engine roster, a tile-production stage, and a resulting communication-unit stage) so the reader can directly compare how each backend differs only in its signaling mechanism and its allocation of SM resources between compute and communication.
summary_zh: 该图比较了 Syncopate 编译器为同一通信调度选择的三种后端实现：(a) 拷贝引擎配合全局内存信号，(b) 专用 SM 驱动传输，(c) 通信与计算共处同一 SM 并使用共享内存屏障，三者结构一致仅信号机制不同。
